items.headline: Senate President Ben Albritton says he'll vote 'no' on property tax cuts
items.blurb: Senate President Ben Albritton now opposes the property tax measure his own chamber voted to put on the ballot, warning it would strip up to a third of the resources rural counties rely on for law enforcement and emergency response. He points to the state Taxation and Budget Reform Commission convening next year as the better venue for a change this large.

items.headline: Amendment 3 is one step toward greater housing affordability
items.blurb: A Florida Realtors leader argues that raising the homestead exemption lowers the cost of owning a home and is a meaningful step toward affordability. The column frames the measure as one piece of a larger housing puzzle rather than a complete fix.

items.headline: Amendment 3 makes a promise Tampa Bay's infrastructure can't keep
items.blurb: A Tampa Bay chamber executive argues the region cannot absorb the revenue loss without falling further behind on roads, water, and storm systems that already need attention. Growth, the column says, is adding pressure at exactly the wrong moment.

items.headline: Amendment 3: It's wrong
items.blurb: Observer Media Group founder Matt Walsh urges a no vote, arguing the measure widens the gap between homestead and other property by shifting more of the burden onto renters, businesses, snowbirds, and new residents. He faults lawmakers for skipping real reform of local government spending.

items.headline: Property tax amendment could cut Manatee County public safety budget
items.blurb: Manatee County Sheriff Rick Wells told a chamber forum his budget would lose tens of millions of dollars in the first year alone, with deeper cuts to follow. A county commissioner criticized how quickly the measure was written and sent to voters.

items.headline: Amendment 3 Losing Support as Republicans Cool and Blacks Flip, St. Pete Poll Finds
items.blurb: A St. Pete Polls survey shows support slipping since the pollster's mid September read, with Republican backing cooling and Black voters moving from support to opposition. Support remains well under the share the amendment needs to pass.

items.headline: The Amendment 3 dilemma: Cut taxes or cut services?
items.blurb: Jacksonville's auditor estimates the city would lose hundreds of millions of dollars a year, roughly a tenth of its operating budget, if the measure passes. The guide lays out the tradeoff between homeowner savings and reduced city services.

items.headline: Questions answered: What Amendment 3 could mean for your property tax bill
items.blurb: Hillsborough County Property Appraiser Bob Henriquez explains that tax bills will not vanish, because school taxes and other fees remain, though the average homeowner could still save a substantial amount once the exemption is fully phased in. He warns that core services would feel the revenue loss first.

items.headline: Why I'm voting yes on Florida's Amendment 3
items.blurb: Miami Dade Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez makes the case for a yes vote, arguing homeowners should not need payment plans to cover a property tax bill. He frames the larger exemption as relief that is long overdue.

items.headline: Will Amendment 3 help or hurt Florida? Depends on whom you ask
items.blurb: Florida Realtors and Florida TaxWatch lay out opposing cases side by side, one calling the measure genuine relief for families and businesses, the other warning it was rushed and may push local governments to raise money elsewhere. The piece includes estimated statewide homeowner savings for the first two years.

items.headline: Multiple polls show declining support for Florida's property tax-cutting Amendment 3
items.blurb: Several independent surveys show support drifting downward and failing to reach the required threshold in any of the state's media markets. The piece notes that the yes campaign's large fundraising advantage has not closed the gap.

items.headline: Poll Finds Amendment 3 Failing to Pass When Voters Informed of Language
items.blurb: A survey commissioned by the Associated Industries of Florida Center for Political Strategy found support falls short of passage once voters hear the actual ballot language and its tradeoffs. Tampa and Miami showed the strongest backing, while Orlando lagged behind.

items.headline: Will Florida's Amendment 3 property tax reduction pass? Polls differ widely
items.blurb: Three recent surveys put support anywhere from the low forties to the low sixties, a spread driven by different survey methods and very differently worded questions. A political scientist quoted in the piece says the outcome is genuinely too close to call.
items.sourceName: South Florida Sun Sentinel via Yahoo News

items.headline: Stetson Poll Shows Donalds, Moody With Leads in Florida Races
items.blurb: A Stetson University survey finds the homestead exemption expansion short of the share it needs to pass, with a large undecided bloc still in play. The same poll shows Republican candidates leading the top statewide races.
